The present appeal is filed by the appellant-Insurance Company challenging the quantum of compensation on the ground that it is on the higher side.
2. The quantum of compensation, injuries sustained and disability suffered by the claimant and fastening of liability on the Insurance Company are not disputed.

From the medical evidence on record i.e., Ex.P.14-discharge summary, it is proved that the claimant has sustained the following injuries:
"Right frontal craniotomy defect.
Communited fracture involving right frontal zygomatic bone and right arbitral roof."

sentences.text:
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation under various heads as follows:
1 Pain and suffering Rs. 50,000/- 2 Medical expenses Rs. 4,20,315/- 3 Nourishment,
attendant & Rs. 20,000/-
conveyance charges 4 Loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/- 5 Loss of future income Rs.
4,40,640/-
5. Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company submitted that the percentage of permanent physical disability held by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
NC: 2024:KHC:50847 P.W.7-doctor is not neurologist, but he is an orthopedic surgeon who cannot assess the mental disability of the claimant.
Therefore, the percentage of disability assessed is on the higher side and that is not properly assessed by the Tribunal.
Therefore, prays to hold the lesser percentage of permanent physical disability and accordingly, prays to reduce the compensation.

6. P.W.7-doctor has assessed the disability of the claimant at 68% contending that the claimant has neurological disability of 25%, psychological/behavioral disability at 8% duration 3 years total global disability is 10%, modern disability at 58%, community disability at 30% and thereby assessed the disability of the claimant towards her whole body at 68%.
7.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained and disability suffered as per the case sheet and discharge summary and other medical records, the claimant has NC: 2024:KHC:50847 suffered both physical and mental disability.
The percentage of disability is not exaggerated one.
The Tribunal has correctly assessed the disability.
Therefore, there is no need to make any interference in this regard.
Therefore, the Tribunal is correct in assessing and considering the percentage of permanent physical disability.
8. Further the Tribunal has granted compensation on other heads, which are on the lower side.
But the claimant has not preferred any appeal.
Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just, proper and correct, which needs no interference.
Therefore, the appeal filed by the claimant is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, it is liable to be dismissed.
Hence, I proceed to pass the following ORDER i.
The appeal is dismissed.
ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 11.12.2012 in MVC.No.4467/2010 passed by XXI Addl.
And Small Causes Judge, and XIX ACMM NC: 2024:KHC:50847 Small Causes Court, Bangalore, is hereby confirmed.
